observation.visible_scene: An outdoor dirt test area under a clear blue sky. On the left stands a fixed launching rig (a tan box, an orange strut, and a pivoting arm painted black then yellow) ending in a large red axe-shaped head. A small reddish object sits on the ground in the center-right. The camera is static throughout; the background treeline and the left box do not shift.
visible_changes: The arm rotates downward from an elevated diagonal angle (t=0) to nearly horizontal (by t~0.4-0.5), carrying the red head from upper-center down to ground level above the reddish object.

Around t=0.56-0.64 a dense white-blue cloud (smoke/powder) suddenly forms at the head's ground position and then continuously expands upward and outward, filling the center and right of the frame by the end.

The solid red head is no longer seen intact after the cloud forms; instead several small red fragments appear, first thrown up and to the left (t~0.7-1.4), later drifting toward the right side of the frame (t~1.4-3.2).
The white-blue cloud keeps growing and rising, with its lower edge spreading along the ground to the right.
From about t=1.6 onward a flat wooden plank is seen tumbling/lying low on the ground to the left of the cloud, moving slightly.
A thin faint streak (smoke trail or wire) appears high in the sky on the right in later frames.
The left launching rig and the tan box remain in place the whole time; only the arm angle and the head/cloud change.
outside_clip_unknowns: What happened before t=0 (how the arm was raised and released).
The cause or nature of the sudden cloud (explosive charge vs. powder/smoke burst) and whether the red head shattered or was a separate target.
The final resting state of the fragments and the cloud after t=3.2.
uncertain_details: Exact identity of the small ground object the head descends toward.
Whether the red airborne pieces are fragments of the axe head or of the ground object.
The precise mechanism producing the cloud (not directly visible).
